capture.final_message:
Treat each side of both equivalences as an independently valid standard martingale fact; then assemble the `Iff`s by ignoring the premise in each direction.

The useful intermediate goals are:

- For the first left-hand statement, show
  \[
  f_n\le f_{n+1}\quad\text{a.e.}
  \]
  The submartingale inequality gives \(f_n\le \mathbb E[f_{n+1}\mid\mathcal G_n]\), while strong adaptedness of the shifted process makes this conditional expectation equal to \(f_{n+1}\). Finite induction and transitivity yield \(f_0\le f_n\).

- For the first right-hand statement, use the conditional Jensen mechanism for the positive-part map:
  \[
  (f_i)^+\le \bigl(\mathbb E[f_j\mid\mathcal F_i]\bigr)^+
  \le \mathbb E[f_j^+\mid\mathcal F_i].
  \]
  The Banach-lattice, solid-norm, and continuity assumptions supply measurability, integrability, monotonicity, and convexity of positive part.

- For the second left-hand statement, unfold the discrete Doob decomposition. The martingale part has increments
  \[
  M_{n+1}-M_n=(f_{n+1}-f_n)
    -\mathbb E[f_{n+1}-f_n\mid\mathcal F_n],
  \]
  whose conditional expectation is zero. Verify adaptedness and integrability, then apply the adjacent-increment characterization of martingales.

- For the second right-hand statement, telescope \(f_j-f_i\). Each later increment has nonnegative conditional expectation at its own time; the tower property and monotonicity transfer this to \(\mathcal G_i\). Summing gives
  \[
  f_i\le\mathbb E[f_j\mid\mathcal G_i],
  \]
  hence the submartingale property.

Finally, prove all four universal assertions once and construct each equivalence as `⟨fun _ ↦ proof_of_rhs, fun _ ↦ proof_of_lhs⟩`.
